author: Khan Academy
description: Join Tim Williams, a former classroom educator and Teacher Resources content creator at Khan Academy, as he explores the tools that let teachers monitor assignment progress using the teacher dashboard. In this video, Tim demonstrates where to find assignment data, how to interpret progress and mastery information, and how to use reports to identify trends. Discover how timely insights can help you respond to student needs and make informed instructional decisions that support student success.
title: Assignment Progress

author: Khan Academy
description:
A low score shouldn’t leave a student stuck on content years below their grade. Khan Academy’s Peter Jacobson explains how Khan Academy's interim assessments place students on learning paths that always include grade-level content, and simply adjust the mix of grade-level and foundational work based on how each student performs. 

To learn more about how to bring Khan Academy’s new interim assessments to your schools, visit: khanacademy.org/schools
title: A Low Score Shouldn’t Mean Falling Behind Your Class

author: Khan Academy
description:
What if an assessment report told you more than a percentile? Sal Khan explains how Khan Academy’s interim assessments ask students to explain their thinking, then give teachers a course customized for each student and a clearer picture of who really understood the idea. 

To learn more about how to bring Khan Academy’s new interim assessments to your schools, visit: khanacademy.org/schools
title: Sal Khan: Assessment Reports That Go Beyond a Percentile

author: Khan Academy
description: A right-or-wrong answer doesn’t tell the whole story. Khan Academy Chief Learning Officer Kristen DiCerbo shares what happened when students explained their thinking in a conversation with Khanductor: 20 to 35% of them revealed they knew more about the topic than their initial score showed. To learn more about how to bring Khan Academy’s new interim assessments to your schools, visit: khanacademy.org/schools
title: 20–35% of Students Knew More Than Their Score Showed

author: Khan Academy
description:
Engineers identify problems by defining criteria for success and constraints on possible solutions. They consider effects on people and the environment, brainstorm ideas collaboratively, and systematically compare designs. This process allows engineers to select promising designs for building and testing.

Sections:
00:00 - A vague problem
01:03 - Identify the problem with criteria and constraints
02:14 - Why precise numbers matter
03:06 - Limits from science, people, and the environment
04:29 - Brainstorm solutions
05:15 - Select a design
06:46 - Putting it all together
